title: ignite-quarterly-ic-ops-brief-and-facilitation-kit-v0-1
content:
Purpose: lightweight facilitation kit + operations brief for the Q2 ignite/all-hands week. Designed for IC-led breakout sessions, rapid OKR input, and an executive update that is friendly to engineering audiences.

Quick context (TL;DR):
- Goal for the week: converge on 3 company-level OKR bets for Q2 2025, validate engineering capacity for two high-risk performance projects (continuous batching improvements + quantization rollout), and rehearse an operational incident response tabletop for a large-hosted API outage.
- Audience: ICs across serving-runtime, product, SRE, and solutions engineering; leadership (execs, VPs) for the executive update slot; ops leads as facilitators.
- Outcome: a prioritized OKR slate (owner + measurable), an annotated risk register, and a runbook draft for the incident exercise.

Pre-work (asks to participants) — send 48–72 hours before session:
- Fill the one-pager: current top broken thing, suggested fix, estimated engineering cost (person-weeks), and impact on latency/cost/user-facing errors. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/ignite-q2-2025-prep.
- Read the quarter retrospective notes (serving-runtime). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/874.
- Bring one concrete prompt/metric that demonstrates a regression or improvement candidate for model serving (e.g., long-context throughput numbers).

Agenda (2.5 hours all-hands ops block)
- 0:00–0:10 Opening (Maya) — framing, what we need to decide, and success criteria for the block.
- 0:10–0:30 Executive micro-update (founders + CTO) — 5 minute bullets each, then 10 minutes rapid Q&A. Suggested slide deck: 7 slides max (metrics-first).
- 0:30–1:10 Breakout 1 (IC-led by team): OKR candidate generation. Template: objective (one line), 3 measurable KRs, risk anchor, rough owner estimate. Each table does 3 submissions.
- 1:10–1:30 Lightning reports (one rep per breakout, 2 mins each) — capture in shared doc.
- 1:30–2:10 Breakout 2 (Deep-dive): two technical bets to validate capacity: continuous batching pipeline improvements (serving-runtime) and quantization rollout automation (platform-engineering). Deliverable: feasibility + go/no-go decision and required gating metrics.
- 2:10–2:30 Incident tabletop (SRE lead): simulate hosted API region failure and evaluate fallback behavior (model routing, cached responses, SLA alerts). Outcome: live edits to incident runbook.

Facilitator notes (short):
- Keep breakout time bounded; use the timer in the shared doc.
- Encourage measurable KRs (percent/absolute numbers) — if a team writes vague KRs, ask: "How will you know we moved the needle?"
- Capture decisions inline with Jira keys (create INF tickets for each adopted KR).
- Encourage cross-team owners for cross-cutting risks (e.g., routing + model variant fallbacks require runtime + platform sign-off).

Draft company-level OKR slate (candidate items collected from pre-rounds and leadership input)
1) Improve end-to-end hosted API p99 tail latency and predictability
   - KR1: Reduce hosted API p99 token latency from current 420ms to <= 320ms for 95% of requests by end of Q2.
   - KR2: Reduce variance in p99 across regions (stdev decrease 30%).
   - KR3: Deploy standardized fallback/variant route so 100% of traffic has an automated fallback path.
   - Owner: eng-serving-runtime (primary) + product-hosted-api (secondary)
   - Risks: regression on cost if batching thresholds mis-tuned (INF-2384).

2) Make Dedicated capacity SLAs predictable for enterprise customers
   - KR1: 99.5% monthly uptime across reserved capacity clusters for customers on Dedicated tiers.
   - KR2: Deliver autoscale policy templates that reduce customer reported capacity incidents by 50%.
   - KR3: Publish public performance playbook and run two customer readouts.
   - Owner: product-dedicated + infra.

3) Reduce serving unit cost for the top-10 latency-sensitive prompts
   - KR1: Reduce per-token compute cost for top-10 prompts by 30% via batching, prefix caching, and quantization.
   - KR2: Automate selection of quantization profiles for 80% of production models without human intervention.
   - KR3: Integrate cost telemetry into Redwood Console and surface per-route recommendations.
   - Owner: optimize + serving-runtime + console-and-tooling.

Notes on measurement: define exact metrics early; for latency targets use synthetic query mix + labeled production sample. Console owners should wire dashboards before mid-quarter check-in.

Executive update outline (3 slides, short talking points):
- Slide 1 — State of the business: net MRR movement, committed Dedicated deals, and notable enterprise pilots. Keep 3 bullets, numbers only.
- Slide 2 — Technical health: p95/p99 trends, SLO burn rates, and top 3 reliability incidents since last quarter.
- Slide 3 — Ask from the org: two big bets (continuous batching + quantization automation), required headcount/slots, and timelines.

Incident tabletop script (short):
- Scenario: regional cloud provider has severe degradation in a primary region during weekday peak. Region A loses 60% capacity for 45 minutes.
- Trigger: automated alerts from Console show increased error rates and p99 regressions; leader decides to route a fraction of traffic to secondary region and to a lower-cost quantized variant.
- Tasks: validate auto-fallback triggers, verify KV cache invalidation won't cause burst spike, identify downstream customer impact.
- Runbook edits to aim for: clearer fallbacks, explicit cross-team escalation points, and pre-approved rollback policy for model rollouts.

Risk register (annotated highlights):
- Cost regression: batching and quantization changes can reduce cost but may cause quality regressions. Mitigation: eval harness + A/B with canary rollback and prompt-set checks.
- Capacity vs SLAs: Dedicated autoscale misconfig could create false assurance for enterprise customers. Mitigation: integrate synthetic traffic tests + capacity alarms.
- Observability gaps: some per-route cost telemetry not surfaced for long-tail customers. Mitigation: console retention increase + templated dashboards.

Decision log (placeholder) — to be populated during the session:
- Adopted company OKRs: [TBD] (create INF tickets for each KR).
- Approved bets: continuous batching scope (Y/N), quantization rollout scope (Y/N).
- Incident runbook acceptance: (Y/N) and owners.

Post-session actions (first 14 days):
- Day 0–2: Consolidate breakout outputs and label candidate OKRs as primary/secondary. Owner: Maya.
- Day 3–7: Create INF tickets for each primary KR and assign owners. Owners: breakout leads.
- Day 7–14: Console teams to wire basic KR dashboards and add alerting thresholds.

Open questions / notes to self (rough):
- How do we weight product-led value vs infrastructure cost savings in OKR prioritization? Recommend a rubric: customer-facing revenue impact (score 1–5) + risk reduction (1–5) + implementation effort (1–5).
- Consider a separate small working group (2 eng + 1 product) to own quantization rollout gate automation.

Appendix: templates (cut/paste into breakout doc)
- OKR template (one line objective, KR1 numeric, KR2 numeric, KR3 numeric, owner(s), leading indicators, required milestones).
- Breakout note-taking template: owner, supporters, blockers, followups (with links to created INF tickets).

Quick links (most relevant):
- Confluence prep page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/ignite-q2-2025-prep
- Related Jira: INF-2384 (batching experiment), INF-2411 (quantization automation scaffold)
- GitHub PR (serving perf): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/874

Footer (tone): keep this lightweight and iterative. This doc is a facilitation kit not the final OKR canon. Expect heavy edits during the week and followups in the OKR tracker.

-- end of facilitation kit --
